scope: Apple SDL native ownership and guest public ABI boundary; supersedes internal allocation mirroring in earlier SDL checkpoint contracts.
native_private_storage: Native SDL retains its original native allocator. Its worker objects, callbacks, opaque structs and64-bit pointers never become guest allocation mirrors.
guest_public_storage: Registered guest callbacks allocate and free public borrowed results. Host snapshots validate read-only guest copies before reuse. Guest SDL_malloc/calloc/realloc/free retain their callback contract. Native internal allocation counts and callback invocations intentionally differ from the mirror implementation.
logging: Messages outside a guest frame are copied with callback identity, userdata, priority and category into a mutex-protected FIFO, then dispatched on the next owner entry. No native worker borrows a guest CPU. Synchronous owner messages remain immediate. Asynchronous delivery timing/thread is adapted.
synchronization: Recursive native SDL mutexes and condition variables use nonreused typed32-bit tokens. A registry reference protects each native call; destruction while held/waiting is rejected. Condition waits require exactly one held mutex level. Null operands retain pinned SDL semantics.
acceptance: Native CoreAudio silent-stream drain is component evidence. Original game sound requires the remaining guest device/stream/data APIs and an actual original mixing run.
apple_driver_selection: The original exact AUDIO_DRIVER hint value directsound is mapped to coreaudio on Apple, with the original priority and real SDL result. Other values retain native failure behavior. SDL_GetHint reports the selected native value.
tls: Guest ID addresses contain nonreused32-bit tokens for host SDL_TLSID objects. Real SDL_GetTLS/SetTLS maintain thread isolation. Native values carry only guest DWORDs and cdecl targets; cleanup runs with the live exiting owner CPU before TEB/stack release, or inside explicit SDL_CleanupTLS/SDL_Quit scopes. Replacement does not invoke the former destructor; a registered destructor is called even for zero data. Mutating TLS during the pinned native cleanup loop stops explicitly. Cross-FLS/SDL destructor resurrection cycles are not accepted.
